children: Asian benzene prices have surged 19% to six-month highs as an indefinite plant shutdown by South Korea's Lotte Chemical comes amid widespread supply constraints across regional refineries, crackers, and reformates, according to OPIS data.
The midpoint of the OPIS FOB Korea benzene assessment climbed 19% to $1,102/mt on Sept. 3 from $925/mt on Aug. 3, according to OPIS data.

The rally was mirrored in China, where domestic ex-tank midpoint climbed 19% to 8,920 yuan/mt from 7,485 yuan/mt over the same period. On an import-parity basis, the price rose to $1,147/mt CFR China from $959/mt, reaching a six-month high.

South Korea's Lotte Chemical shut its naphtha-fed steam cracker and associated aromatics production at Daesan on Sept. 1 as scheduled, with the shutdown expected to be indefinite, removing 220,000 mt/year of benzene capacity at a time when regional supply is already tight, according to industry sources.

The loss of Lotte's benzene output comes as Asian availability has tightened across multiple production routes, with supply from steam crackers constrained by poor economics and reduced operating rates, while refinery- and paraxylene-linked benzene production has also remained limited.

A major South Korean producer is operating its selective toluene disproportionation, or STDP, unit at around 80% of capacity, according to an industry source. Its operating rate is however expected to increase in September alongside the scheduled maintenance shutdown of the producer's No. 1 PX unit.
Outside China, refinery-based benzene production also remains constrained despite relatively stable overall refinery operating rates.

Strong gasoline blending margins and favorable octane economics have incentivized refiners to maximize gasoline output rather than aromatics production, restricting incremental benzene availability. Although the Strait of Hormuz remains closed, refiners have managed to maintain relatively stable operating rates after diversifying crude procurement following the initial disruption from the conflict.
The switch to alternative crude grades, however, has created operational challenges for refineries designed around Middle Eastern crude slates, limiting their ability to maximize throughput.

Concurrently, Chinese import demand has strengthened alongside the rally as low cargo arrivals and recovering consumption from downstream derivatives draw down commercial stocks. Coastal China benzene inventories fell by 8,000 mt week on week to 45,000 mt this week, according to CMA data.

The reduced inventory cushion has encouraged traders and downstream consumers to secure material ahead of further tightening, while some Chinese refiners have continued to favor gasoline blending over aromatics extraction.

Competition for October-loading cargoes has consequently intensified. Spot import deals into China were concluded at premiums in the low-to-mid $60s/mt over the weekly FOB Korea average this week, up from premiums in the mid-to-high $50s/mt a week earlier, reflecting firm Chinese demand and limited regional spot availability.

The plant shutdown forms part of a wider consolidation of Lotte Chemical and HD Hyundai Chemical's Daesan petrochemical assets as South Korea restructures its naphtha-cracking sector amid persistent overcapacity and weak production economics. Lotte Chemical spun off its Daesan operations into Lotte Daesan Petrochemical, which is being combined with HD Hyundai Chemical, with Lotte Chemical and HD Hyundai Oilbank each holding a 50% stake in the integrated entity.

Against that backdrop, Lotte Chemical and HD Hyundai Chemical's jointly operated styrene monomer facilities at Daesan are expected to remain adequately supplied with benzene from HD Hyundai Chemical's existing production, limiting the need to replace Lotte's lost output directly through spot purchases.
HD Hyundai Chemical can produce 705,000 mt/year of benzene at its Daesan complex in South Chungcheong province, according to CMA data.

As a result, the more significant impact of Lotte's closure is expected to be felt in South Korea's merchant balance, with fewer surplus barrels potentially available for external sale and exports even as Chinese import demand remains firm.
Additional South Korean benzene supply is expected next year when S-Oil starts its new cracker and associated 272,000 mt/year benzene unit, currently expected in early 2027.
